feature: Owner-bound earlier-message SDK forks from the selected Pi history

red.finding: The SDK history guard cancelled an earlier-message fork.

retainedDevelopmentFailures.finding: A queued follow-up had no checkpoint at its selected point. A later accepted prefix now attests the selected history, carrying only a system checkpoint for configuration validation.

Clone, compact, then fork into inherited history lost the old configuration owner. New checkpoints retain the Pi owner; legacy owner inference requires a matching configuration hash in existing receipts. The fingerprint guard was not relaxed.

The external replay peer omitted SDK result user-message UUID acknowledgements, so the steering case could not settle. The peer now reports consumed input UUIDs; this was not a production provider change.
The new filesystem counter covered the probe but not the extra tool. The fixture now records both actual executions; the extra tool had executed normally.

Codex and Opus passed queued forks. Haiku ran the requested bounded wait using a shell variable to build its path, but the test required a contiguous absolute path and never released its gate. The matcher now recognizes the scoped gate basename. All three passed the corrected rerun without a provider-code change.
retainedDevelopmentFailures.cloneRegression: All three real-model clone cases passed in this retained run.
